memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord regretted that he had made human beings on the earth, and his heart was deeply troubled. - Gen 6:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a stunning glimpse into the heart of God. Human sin does not leave Him cold and indifferent. It says His "heart was deeply troubled" - literally, filled with pain. The Lord grieved over what His creation had become. Sin is not merely the breaking of a rule; it is the wounding of a relationship, and it brings sorrow to the heart of God.

We must be careful here. When it says God "regretted," it does not mean He made a mistake or changed His eternal nature; God does not change His mind as we do (Num 23:19). Rather, this is God speaking in language we can understand, showing us the real grief that sin causes Him. Our sin genuinely pains the heart of our Maker.

What a tender picture this gives us of God. He is not a distant, unfeeling force. He is a Father whose heart aches over the ruin of His children. He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked (Ezek 33:11).

This same grieving love is what we see supremely at the cross. Jesus wept over a city that rejected Him (Luke 19:41), and He bore in His own body the sin that grieves God's heart. When you are tempted to think your sin doesn't matter, remember: it grieves the heart of the God who loves you. And when you turn back to Him, you turn back to a Father longing to welcome you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you realise that your sin grieves the heart of God who loves you?
- How does God's grief over sin change the way you see it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for treating lightly what grieves Your heart. Thank You that Your love for me is so deep that my sin causes You pain. Draw me back to You.
